summary: Laclede County tower built in early 1937 by a CCC crew for the Roubidoux District. A 1946 survey note places it standing; the page marks it removed, with no date.

facts.design: All-steel frame with a concrete foundation; the stairs and platforms are not steel
facts.status_note: The Central US Lookouts page marks the tower removed, with no date. No source we found describes the site now.

events.note: Erected by a crew from the Lynchburg CCC camp; a Houston Herald item dated January 28, 1937 calls it the third all-steel, 100-foot tower in the Roubidoux District
National Geodetic Survey station description (1946) measures from the Forest Service lookout tower, which it calls the Gulf lookout tower

notes_for_editor: Built date rests on a January 1937 Houston Herald item quoted on the Central US Lookouts page; the newspaper itself was not fetched. The 1946 survey note calls the tower the Gulf lookout tower and implies it stood then, but no source says outright that it is the 1937 structure. The 1937 item names the Gardner National Forest; no source we read explains that name. Wikipedia gives two dates for the 1939 proclamation (text: September 11; infobox: September 23). The ebandflo.org Missouri Lookout Towers Inventory did not resolve (DNS error) and the Missouri Life article returned 403, so neither was checked. Removal date unknown. Height 30.5 m matches the 100-foot figure in the 1937 item.
